results.title: How does Modal pricing work for training and fine-tuning? | Nodus Blog
results.author: Nodus Compute Engineering
highlights:
Nodus Compute Engineering Nov 6, 2026 · 8 min read

...

Nov 6, 2026 - 9 min read 

Modal bills a training run per second across three meters, GPU, CPU cores and memory, and multiplies the sum by 1.15x or 1.75x if you pin a region. Nodus lists the same NVIDIA H100 at $2.60/hr on its pricing page, against $3.95/hr for Modal’s GPU meter alone, and restores your checkpoint when a machine is reclaimed. On Modal, a preempted run that starts over is billed again, so checkpointing is part of the price.

...

## What does Modal charge for while a training job runs?

Modal bills each running container for three things at once. The GPU meter is the big one, and CPU and memory are charged on top of it, per second, at the amounts you request or actually use, whichever is higher.

| Meter | Modal list rate | Per hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | $0.001097 / sec | $3.9492 |
| NVIDIA B200 | $0.001736 / sec | $6.2496 |
| NVIDIA A100 80 GB | $0.000694 / sec | $2.4984 |
| CPU, per physical core (2 vCPU) | $0.0000131 / sec | $0.04716 |
| Memory, per GiB | $0.00000222 / sec | $0.007992 |
| Volumes | $0.09 per GiB-month, first 1 TiB free | |
| Network egress | $0.04 per GiB beyond the plan’s included amount | |

Prices checked November 6, 2026, from modal.com/pricing. Hourly figures are the per-second rates times 3,600.

Two details on that page are easy to miss. Each container has a minimum request of 0.125 cores and 128 MiB, and you pay for the higher of what you request and what you use. Modal also says it may run a `gpu="H100"` request on an H200, or a `gpu="A100"` request on an 80 GB A100, without changing the price. A `gpu="B200+"` request is billed as B200 even when it lands on a B300 (GPU guide).

...

Nodus quotes compute per machine instead of per meter, so a GPU’s hourly rate already includes the CPU and memory that come with it. The H100 SXM is listed at $2.60/hr on the Nodus pricing page and the B200 at $5.50/hr, and our docs say the rate is frozen when capacity is acquired (usage and costs).

results.title: Free GPU hours on Modal: what $30 a month really buys
highlights:
Modal's free Starter plan includes $30 of GPU compute a month. See how many hours each GPU gets you, what quietly eats them, and how to host a coding model.

By TechTipsEasy · November 3, 2026 · 10 min read

Modal, a serverless GPU cloud, gives every workspace on its free Starter plan $30 of compute every month. GPUs are billed by the second and apps can scale to zero, so that credit turns into real GPU time: about 6.6 hours on an H200, 12 hours on an A100 80 GB or 37 hours on an L4.

...

## How many GPU hours $30 buys

Modal's pricing page lists GPU prices per second. Multiply by 3,600 for the hourly rate, then divide $30 by it:

| GPU | GPU memory | Price per hour | Hours for $30 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H200 | 141 GB | $4.54 | 6.6 |
| H100 | 80 GB | $3.95 | 7.6 |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 96 GB | $3.03 | 9.9 |
| A100 80 GB | 80 GB | $2.50 | 12.0 |
| A100 40 GB | 40 GB | $2.10 | 14.3 |
| L40S | 48 GB | $1.95 | 15.4 |
| A10 | 24 GB | $1.10 | 27.2 |
| L4 | 24 GB | $0.80 | 37.5 |
| T4 | 16 GB | $0.59 | 50.8 |

Treat these as ceilings. CPU cores and memory are metered alongside the GPU, so a real workload gets a little less. Pinning containers to a region multiplies prices by 1.15 to 1.75, so leave placement to Modal unless you need it. One small bonus: according to Modal's GPU guide, a plain `gpu="H100"` request may run on an H200 at no extra cost.

...

Prices and docs checked November 3, 2026. Modal can change its plans, prices and free credits at any time.
